cities.d: political capital of Malawi and the seat of government

x.around: The town is very spread out so getting around can be a bit of a chore. You can pick up taxis from the Lilongwe Hotel (in the Old Town) and the Capital Hotel (in the Capital City). If you're feeling adventurous, you can take a minibus. It's very cheap (1000-2000 K as of August 2024), but you will be getting very familiar with your fellow passengers.

hidden.d: See the traditional Malawian dancing and traditional Malawian drumming. Includes live acoustic Malawian music and traditional Malawian dinner.
Forbidden to enter on premises but you can peek the buildings from the entrance gate.

n.en: World War I Memorial tower and statue of Hastings Kamuzu Banda

hidden.d: It is back down towards old town by the bridge over the river, look out for the sign. It is a wildlife rescue and rehabilitation centre that provides excellent tours of the centre and its wilderness zone, a wide range of wildlife…
Mausoleum of Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda, first president of independent Malawi.

x.intro: Lilongwe is the capital of Malawi. It's a very green city, to the extent that sometimes you wonder if there is a city centre at all as buildings in the new town at least are divided by patches of grassy land and trees.

next.d: a laid-back village on the south end of Lake Malawi.
the eastern gateway to Zambia, 1-2 hours away
a fantastic wildlife reserve in Zambia. Kiboko Safaris (see Kiboko Town Hotel in Sleep section of this page) and possibly a few others run roundtrip excursions to the park, and with advance notice…

x.safe: Transport is not always easy to get at late hours of the night so always make sure you have means of transport to getting back to where you're staying. Taxis are available. Lilongwe is said to be unsafe at night so don't walk alone after dark.

cities.d: economic capital and largest city with an interesting downtown, decent nightlife and music, a range of hotels from the elegant to resthouses, and a vibrant street and market culture

x.around: For the budget traveller there are basically two ways of getting around Blantyre: by foot or by minibus.

hidden.d: One of the oldest buildings in Blantyre and has spacious grounds with a children's playground. Houses the La Caverna Art Gallery, with great carvings and a museum section upstairs.

must.d: The national museum of Malawi. Artifacts includes a royal ceremonial stool from the 16th century and an exhibition of traditional dances, the Gule Wamkulu.
Described as the first permanent church between the Zambezi and the Nile, this church was designed by David Scott, a Scottish missionary, with help of local workers.

n.de: Saint Michael and All Angels Kirche, Blantyre, Malawi
n.en: St. Michael and All Angels Church

x.safe: Night time muggings or robberies do occur. Private taxis are cheap and readily available. Ask around and bargain.

cities.d: charming town not far from the intriguing Misuku Hills and a short distance from Lake Malawi and growing quickly since the 2009 opening of a uranium mine

x.intro: Karonga is a city in northern Malawi located on the coast of Lake Nyasa.

must.d: The biggest attraction to Karonga is this museum, which has great exhibitions about dinosaurs, including the famous Malawisaurus. The permanent exhibition "Dinosaurs to Democracy," takes visitors through the history of the region.

intro: Malawi (Chichewa: Malaŵi, Chitumbuka: Malaŵi) is a small, landlocked country in Africa whose eastern border mostly follows Lake Malawi, the third largest lake on the continent. It's described as the "Warm Heart of Africa", referring to the friendliness of the people.

other.d: laid back fishing village on the tip of a peninsula jutting out into the southern portion of Lake Malawi.

x.around: The drive to Cape Maclear from Monkey Bay is through beautiful sunlit forest, preserved Lake Malawi National Park, which extends into the Lake, including nine islands, and offers shelter to some of the most spectacular fish in Africa.

hidden.d: On the north end of town. These are the final resting places of the first missionaries to the area, who died in 1875.

x.intro: Cape Maclear (aka Chembe) is a small fishing village, composed of 6 smaller villages, on Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi) in Malawi. It has tarmac road leading into (and straight out of) town. The village along a dirt road with many paths leading to the lake and to the outskirts of the village.

next.d: if you've got a little bit sunburnt, you can head south to the former capital of Malawi, and a beautiful, wooded mountain-town that feels very little like Africa.

other.d: and Chizumulu Islands - great aquatic life and a back door to Mozambique. These islands are only reachable to tourists by private boat or the public ferry which only runs 1-2 times each week and is…

x.around: A moto-taxi ride from the ferry terminal to the western coast should cost around 3000 K.

hidden.d: Small museum with few artifacts and explanations. As of August 2024, the museum is undergoing a refurbishing and should be completed within the next months.
Richly decorated luxury private house owned by Green Safaris. Sometimes rented by groups, the house can only be visited when there are no guests.
Dates back from early 1900s. The building with an adjacent cloister is surprisingly big for this small island.The security guards will propose you to climb the tower for the panoramic views.
Concave boulder which rings like a bell when hit by a stone. The self-proclaimed "guardians" of the rock from the nearby village will guide you and ask you 5000 K for their community.

x.intro: Likoma Island, along with its sister Chizumulu Island, is in the Mozambican territorial waters of Lake Malawi/Nyasa. Both Likoma Island and Chizumulu belong to Malawi.

other.d: Mua is a village in the Dedza District of Malawi, close to the Dedza Plateau.

x.intro: Mua Village, Mua Mission and the KuNgoni Centre of Culture and Art are in the Dedza district of Malawi.

other.d: a popular large village as you head up the Lake Road from Mangochi toward Cape Maclear

x.intro: Monkey Bay is at the southern end of Lake Malawi (Lake Nyasa), in the Southern Region of Malawi. It is a small port town, home to large monkey population and gateway to Cape Maclear and the world heritage listed Lake Malawi National Park.

other.d: a rocky bay towards the north of the lake - check into one of the lodges and you could be here for a while

x.around: Nkhata Bay is fairly small and walkable. Alternatively, you can hire a water taxi to take you from one end of the village to the other; this is also a neat way to see the coastline. Most of the hostels and hotels also have vehicles and you can usually hitch a ride when they head into town for supplies.
x.intro: Nkhata Bay is a small, bustling fishing village of about 15,000 inhabitants, located about 50 kilometers from Mzuzu. Straddling the steep, verdant mountains of Malawi's rift valley, Nkhata Bay overlooks the lake like a lord overlooks his manor.
x.safe: As with most places be careful walking at night and do not carry all your cash with you, especially walking between the town and the lodges to the south. A frequent problem is Rastas trying to sell marijuana who are working with police to shake down tourists for bribes.

other.d: 550 km² of unspoiled forest along the shores of the Shire River. The national park is best approached from the town of Liwonde.

x.safe: If staying at Mvuu Camp or Mvuu Lodge, then be very careful if you need to leave your accommodation at night. Encounters with hippos are all too easy as they graze on the lawn in front of the chalets at night!

x.around: You can do game drives through the lodges in the park or you can self-drive. The Reserve is committed to the environment so there are no tarmac roads and the number of artificial bridges is kept to a minimum. Because of this, you will need a 4x4 vehicle for getting around the reserve. You can rent a vehicle in Blantyre.
x.intro: Majete Wildlife Reserve is in the Chikwawa District of Malawi.
